Adolion: The Saga
Author view
Overview
Memory
⚑
Where you are
The Night After the Trial
The night after the Trial, the house is dark and still, and somewhere below a servants' door that should be barred clicks shut.
The scene is tense.
About this story
The whole of Adolion, played as one long campaign. You start as a new adventuring party at the Guild in Aegis City, with Belle and Dalan beside you, and every posting you take, every house you serve and every friend you make is carried forward into the next. The roads out of Aegis City are yours to choose, and the choices add up. Make your persona the heir of House Nightriver who has chosen the adventurer's life, with a spark of the family's magic. Keep the house's secrets out of the persona's description: every character in the scene reads it.
Recently
You left Trial by Combat behind and moved into The Night After the Trial.
Leevon charged before the Saintess could finish her decree, and Max Nightriver met him with blade and magic, disarming him and sending him crashing into the dirt to win the Trial. High Saintess Merryn stood motionless with her hand outstretched toward the fallen lance as the court fell into absolute silence. Ronan watched with his hand on his rapier, coiled and waiting for the rules to break entirely.
Open threads
Who opened the servants' door at the Nightriver Estate that night, and what they intend.
What Lord Javon means to say or do now that he has approached Max after the Trial's collapse.
What the Inquisition's investigation into Leevon's conduct and the envenomed lance will uncover, and who armed him.
What Lord Javon intends in approaching Max now that the Trial has collapsed.
Your story
Wendhope and Driftmere — The party told Baroness Serenola the truth of the Driftmere mine; she paid them, kept it closed, and wrote to the Nightriver estate. Lord Javon's letter summoned the heir home, and the party rode for the Nightriver Estate at nightfall.
Now: House Nightriver
This chapter
Baroness Serenola accepted the party's account of the Driftmere mine, paid the promised gold, kept the mine closed, and wrote to the Nightriver estate that the heir had succeeded where the house would not have. Max Nightriver received Lord Javon's cold letter commanding his immediate return, and the party rode from Driftmere to the nearly empty Nightriver Estate during the mid-year recess.

Welden crossed the heir's path, jumpier than usual and unwilling to explain why. Max went to Father's study, where Lord Javon revealed the Driftmere mine was declared dead and that the Inquisition had sent a letter questioning the reported demons. Javon ordered Max to stand as the Crown's Second against General Leevon in a Trial by Combat in three days, warning that refusal would leave the house unprotected. Max accepted and left the study, then found Shiya in the corridor, who reported three cloaked visitors had come asking only for Max and left a blackened coin. When Max asked who came through the servants' door at night, Shiya named Duchess Eriana Valtara, who had been slipping in after midnight for the past week without informing the main household. Shiya confirmed that Natalia was the one meeting Eriana in the second-floor drawing room each night, and Natalia herself stepped forward to admit the visits, saying they concerned her future and the seals. That night Max hid by the servants' door and watched Natalia let Eriana inside; when Max confronted her, Natalia deflected, claiming they were discussing diplomacy, and Shiya intervened to counsel discretion. Max let the matter rest, and three days later rode to the lists to take his place as the Crown's Second. Natalia warned him the rules had been changed to allow lethal blows, and when General Leevon lowered his lance, Max caught it and revealed venom coating the dragon-bone.
